attrs.description: Spotify's closed-loop, first-party promotion stack inside Spotify for Artists: Marquee, Showcase, Discovery Mode, and free editorial playlist pitching.

key_facts.claim: Marquee: full-screen sponsored recommendation of a new release shown to Free and Premium listeners on app open/Home; targets listeners based on listening history, not demographics; reporting covers listens, saves, playlist adds from exposed listeners; Spotify claims exposed listeners are >2x more likely to save/add and 3x more likely to stream the artist's other releases

Showcase: mobile banner card at the top of Spotify's Home feed with 7 customizable headlines (new music, recently released, on tour, release anniversary, getting buzz, seasonal vibes, releasing music soon); up to 14-day runtime
Spotify claims Showcase viewers are 6x more likely to stream the promoted release

Discovery Mode: increased likelihood of selected tracks being recommended in Radio, Autoplay, and algorithmic mixes; Spotify claims +50% saves, +44% playlist adds, +37% follows in the first month, and 31% of DM listeners brand-new to the artist
Playlist pitching (free, fourth Kit tool): submit unreleased music >=7 days before release for editorial playlist consideration; delivers a decision (accepted/declined) but no paid mechanics

Audience segmentation engine: six official segments - super / moderate / light listeners (active last 28 days by intensity), previously active (lapsed 28+ days), programmed (heard only via playlists/radio), potential (never heard, profile match)

Eligibility gates: Marquee requires 5,000 monthly active listeners in target markets and billing country in a supported market; Showcase/display campaigns require >=1,000 streams in the last 28 days in at least one target market
key_facts.note: Marquee 5k-MAL and Showcase 1k-stream gates per Chartlex 2026 compilation of official docs

key_facts.claim: Discovery Mode eligibility: >=3 eligible songs, >=25,000 monthly listeners, >=20 streams per song in Discovery Mode contexts in the last 28 days, plus 30 days on platform

Marquee/Showcase targeting automation: Spotify selects listeners most likely to stream after seeing the ad; suppression of already-converted listeners is automatic; no public cross-advertiser auction documented - CPC is posted/set by Spotify, not bid-based

Discovery Mode: artist flags priority songs; Spotify's recommendation systems increase their likelihood of being served in Radio/Autoplay/mixes; increases likelihood but does not guarantee placement, and does not affect editorial playlists

All campaign, billing, targeting, and listening data lives on Spotify's infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform (2016 migration from owned data centers; stack: Pub/Sub, Dataflow, BigQuery, Dataproc, Bigtable/Cloud Storage/Compute Engine); the listener-affinity graph never leaves Spotify's tenant; artist-visible data surfaces only through Spotify for Artists
Marquee money path: $100 minimum budget per (sub-)campaign, CPC ~$0.55-$1.50 (Chartlex 2026 campaign data; older reports ~$0.50); 10-day window; pay only for clicks; unspent budget is not charged
key_facts.note: $100 minimum confirmed in official docs; CPC range from Chartlex 2026

key_facts.claim: Showcase money path: $100 minimum; CPC typically ~$0.40 (chartlex-cited data); 14-day window

Discovery Mode money path: $0 cash; 30% commission on recording royalties from streams of selected songs in Discovery Mode contexts only, deducted from future statements; at a ~$3-$5 per 1,000 streams royalty baseline, 1,000 DM streams net ~$2.10-$3.50 vs. $3-$5

Discovery Mode subtlety: the 30% commission applies to DM-context streams whether or not the algorithm would have served the track there anyway - tracks with existing Radio/Autoplay traffic pay a discount on listening they already had
Unit economics: at ~$0.003-$0.005/stream, one $0.50 Marquee click needs ~100-167 streams to pay back in royalties - the tool only makes sense as fan-acquisition spend, not royalty ROI

$100 at $0.55 CPC = ~180 targeted clicks inside the app, one tap from the music, from listeners with demonstrated affinity - versus Meta's ~$0.15-$0.25 per click-through that still must cross the app boundary; the Kit monetizes Spotify's distribution bottleneck (the November 2025 'modern payola' class-action complaint alleges exactly this dynamic)

Genuinely proprietary (cannot rebuild): the listener-affinity graph (petabyte-scale behavioral data on Spotify's GCP tenant), the ad inventory itself (app-open full screen, Home-feed banner), and the algorithmic boost in Radio/Autoplay/mixes - no third party can serve a Marquee or trigger Discovery Mode's ranking signal
key_facts.source: report section A8 (synthesis of official docs + infrastructure facts)

key_facts.claim: Rebuildable at zero cost: audience segmentation logic (super/moderate/light/lapsed/potential) trivially replicable from first-party data; CPC billing mechanics standard; reporting approximated with UTM-tagged smart links + Spotify for Artists source-of-stream data; replicate the measurement discipline (segment, suppress converted, track downstream saves/catalog halo) with free tools - reach and algorithmic leverage are unreplicable

tags_authored.why: unit economics only work as fan-acquisition spend

attrs.description: Paid social campaigns on Facebook/Instagram running the standard Campaign -> Ad Set -> Ad structure on the Meta auction, using the ad -> Pixel-equipped smart link -> Spotify funnel.

key_facts.claim: Deliverables: impressions/clicks on Facebook/Instagram (primarily Reels, Feed, Stories) optimized toward a custom conversion (smart-link click-through to Spotify); Ads Manager reporting on spend, reach, CPM, CPC, cost per conversion

Benchmark funnel (Tier 1 markets, 2026): $0.15-$0.25 per Spotify click-through (good-great), $0.03-$0.08 effective cost per stream, CPM $8-$15; correct funnel structure yields 35-45% higher click-to-stream conversion than direct-to-Spotify ads (Chartlex, 2,400+ campaigns)

Critical caveat: 'A Meta conversion is not a Spotify stream.' Meta records the click-through; what happens inside Spotify (skip, full play, save, follow) is invisible to Meta and differs wildly per listener - but those in-app actions feed Spotify's recommendation engine

The auction (per impression): Total Value = (Advertiser Bid x Estimated Action Rate) + User Value/Ad Quality; highest total value wins - not highest bid; pricing is second-price-like (VCG), so winners pay below their bid

Estimated Action Rate = est. CTR x est. click-to-conversion probability, predicted from the user's full behavior history, time-of-day/device patterns, session context, and cross-platform activity; bid strategies: Lowest Cost, Cost Cap, Bid Cap, ROAS Target
Learning/optimization loop: the ad set needs conversion volume to exit learning (~1,000 conversions/month cited as the practical requirement); minimum viable music test is $10/day for 7-14 days
key_facts.note: agency pricing/resting on a single secondary video source; treat as indicative

key_facts.claim: Agent-like practitioner workflow: prospecting ad sets (lookalike/interest) -> smart link -> retargeting ad set (visitors minus converters) with new creative -> lookalike expansion as seeds grow; retargeting converts at 2-3x cold
The music-specific hack: ad -> Pixel-equipped smart link -> Spotify funnel, because no Pixel can live on Spotify - the fundamental constraint of music campaigns
Pixel events (browser): PageView on smart-link landing; custom conversion on Spotify redirect-URL pageview; optional deeper events (pre-save, merch purchase)

Conversions API (server): event_name, event_time, event_id (dedupe vs. browser), action_source, user_data with SHA-256 hashed email/phone and raw fbp/fbc/IP/user-agent; Event Match Quality below ~5.0 means the server path contributes little; Pixel+CAPI yields 15-25% more attributed conversions

Attribution default: 7-day click + 1-day view (+1-day engage-through for likes/comments/5-sec video views since the 2026 model change); selectable at ad-set level; window choice changes reported numbers, not delivery
iOS ATT reality: ~80%+ opt-out means view-through attribution is largely unavailable on iOS; a meaningful share of reported conversions are modeled, not measured, with no flag distinguishing them

All event, audience, and delivery data lives on Meta's servers (Ads Manager/Events Manager); the advertiser's only owned assets are the smart-link page and its server logs, plus any CAPI endpoint they run; hashed identifiers are sent to Meta for identity-graph matching

Self-serve money path: pure auction; Tier-1 CPC $0.40-$0.80 good / $0.20-$0.40 great; cost per Spotify click-through $0.25-$0.50 good / $0.15-$0.25 great; effective cost per stream $0.08-$0.15 good / $0.03-$0.08 great; Tier 2/3 markets cut costs 40-60% but Spotify payouts are lower there too
Managed services: agencies charge 10-20% of ad spend or $1,500-$8,000+/month retainers; managed beats DIY around $1,500+/mo spend
key_facts.note: evidence gap: rests on a single secondary video source; treat as indicative

key_facts.claim: Unit economics: at $0.20 per Spotify click-through and ~$0.004/stream royalty, the stream alone never pays back the click (~50 streams per click needed); the economics only work if a fraction of acquired listeners become savers/followers who generate algorithmic compounding - you are buying seeds for Spotify's algorithm, not streams

Genuinely proprietary: Meta's identity/behavior graph (the Estimated Action Rate predictor trained on billions of users), the auction and its inventory, and modeled attribution - no open-source stack reproduces 'find people statistically likely to click through to Spotify'

Rebuildable at zero cost: self-hosted landing page (any static host) with open-source analytics snippet (e.g., self-hosted Plausible/Matomo) tracking pageview -> Spotify-click events; manual UTM tagging; lookalike logic approximated by manually finding similar artists' audiences; retargeting via email capture on the landing page (own the list instead of renting the pool); CAPI is just HTTPS POSTs - anyone can implement it, but Meta's matching identity graph on the other end is not replicable

tags_authored.why: buys seeds for Spotify's algorithm, not streams

attrs.description: Two-sided pay-for-review (not pay-for-placement) machines: SubmitHub, Groover, Playlist Push, SoundCampaign - curator consideration + written feedback, enforced by SLAs and a credit ledger.

key_facts.claim: What is sold is a review, not a placement: curator consideration + written feedback; placement is the curator's independent decision - the legal/ToS line that keeps them clear of payola rules

SubmitHub: premium credits ~$0.80-$1.00 each (100 for $80; bulk discounts); 1-3 credits per curator typical, 4-credit top tier new in 2026; typical 30-50 submission campaign = $30-$80; credits never expire; free Standard credits (2 per 4 hours) for testing
SubmitHub premium response SLA: SOURCES DISAGREE - 48 hours (submitlink.io) vs 72 hours (musicinminnesota, letssubmit); likely tier-dependent after the 2026 tier rework
key_facts.note: evidence gap: flag rather than resolve; see https://www.musicinminnesota.com/best-spotify-playlist-service/

key_facts.claim: SubmitHub approvals: average ~24% all outlets, ~29% Spotify playlisters (Dynamoi citing 2025 data); free premium-credit routes: Hot or Not, Verified Reviewers, referrals

Groover: 2 Grooviz = EUR 2 per contact; top-tier 4-6 Grooviz; packs from EUR 46 with up to 20-24% volume discount; practical minimum ~EUR 100 (50 curators as Groover recommends); guaranteed listening + written feedback within 7 days or credits back; 90% reply rate; also connects to labels/radio/journalists

Playlist Push: from $280; example $630 to reach 79 playlists; average ~$450; price varies by genre/curators; genre-matching automation; purchases final, unused budget -> account credit; Artist Protection Fund auto-refunds unfulfilled reviews; detailed report 30 days after campaign if Spotify for Artists is connected
SoundCampaign: from $80; Sept 2026 estimator: $150 -> ~17 projected curator reviews; pay only per completed review; budget can split across Spotify, TikTok creators, and Meta ads

Two-sided unit economics: artist pays ~$1-9 per human review; curator earns $1-$5 per review (SubmitHub, by tier/traffic); the platform keeps the spread plus breakage on unused credits/balances; curator payouts are the platform's COGS; margin is in aggregation - placements cannot be bought without violating Spotify's ToS, so the sellable unit is guaranteed human attention
Playlist Push / SoundCampaign curator payout rates: only dated (2019, ~$0.75/review) or third-party figures; current platform-side payout schedules are not public

Structural comparison: stream-target services instead sell a defined stream target (e.g., from $129 one-time or $149-$999/mo) verifiable in Spotify for Artists - headline prices are not comparable across the two structures

Trust & safety: SubmitHub free AI Song Checker (labels/blocks likely-AI tracks at 85%+), Groover self-declare checkbox + curator opt-out tags, Playlist Push monitoring for fake/inactive followers and multiple accounts, curator tiering with demotion for lapsed standards (SubmitHub 2026: 4-credit top tier is earned, 30-day grace before demotion)

Matching: genre-tag similarity + historical acceptance data route tracks to curators (Playlist Push, SoundCampaign); filter sliders and genre-match scores assist manual selection (SubmitHub); none publish a true ML model - it is rules + historical stats

Data moat: all submission, decision, feedback, pricing-tier, and reputation data lives on each platform's own servers; artists see only their own dashboards, curators only their queues; the cross-artist acceptance-rate dataset and curator reliability scores are the platforms' private moat; marketplaces have no independent stream measurement - downstream verification happens on Spotify's infrastructure via Spotify for Artists

ROI logic: independent playlist placements generate real streams -> saves/follows -> feed Spotify's algorithmic systems (Release Radar, Discover Weekly, Radio); paid curator access buys seeds for algorithmic compounding; low-quality/botted playlists produce streams Spotify may discount or penalize - manipulation can get music removed (Playlist Push's own warning)
Feedback as product: even declined submissions return written curator feedback - market intelligence on why a track isn't landing, reused across campaigns

Genuinely proprietary: the vetted curator network (thousands of relationships, historical acceptance/reliability data, tiering) and the SLA/refund trust infrastructure - you cannot conjure 3,000 responsive curators with track records; the platforms' cross-artist dataset is their compounding data moat

Rebuildable at zero cost: curator discovery via Spotify playlist search + Instagram/TikTok + blog hunting (this is what SubmitHub's directory productizes); outreach via spreadsheet CRM + templated personalized emails + tracking sheet; SLA guarantee as personal follow-up cadence; genre-match filtering by manual listening - DIY costs time instead of $1-$9/review; an indie team with 10-20 hours can replicate a $100 SubmitHub campaign's mechanics (but not instant access to curators who already trust the platform's queue)

attrs.description: Boutique and agency music publicists: skilled human labor (strategy, media-list building, pitching, follow-ups, reporting) plus access to rented data (Muck Rack/Cision media databases, wires, reactive-pitch feeds).

key_facts.claim: Deliverables: press coverage - reviews, features, interviews, premieres, playlist/blog placements; a press kit/bio (often an upfront fee); monthly reporting of clippings with outlet reach; budget blog-PR firms promise volume (Independent Music Promotions: month-to-month $895, typically 12+ reviews/month)
No ethical PR agency can guarantee independent editorial coverage

Metrics: number of placements, outlet reach/readership, share of voice vs. competitors, sentiment, message pull-through; legacy metric AVE (advertising value equivalency) still auto-calculated by tools like Muck Rack but rejected by AMEC's Barcelona Principles 4.0 and banned by CIPR (2017)
Measurement guidance: replace AVE with sentiment trajectory, message pull-through, share of voice, and coverage quality weighted by outlet relevance - a big number in the wrong outlet is worthless

Media database is rented: Cision (1M+ journalist contacts, full PR suite - database, distribution, monitoring, analytics; expensive, annual contracts, complex) or Muck Rack (journalist profiles, pitch tracking, monitoring, AI list building; added press-release distribution in 2025)

Pitching engine is human labor: personalized pitches, follow-up sequences, relationship management - the core labor; Muck Rack's pitch tracking + AI list building automate the plumbing, not the pitch itself

Reactive pitching: HARO (now Connectively - free, journalists come to you, but reactive/competitive/no targeting) and paid feeds: Qwoted (free: 2 pitches/mo with 2-hour delay; Pro $149/mo), Featured.com (free: 3 submissions/mo; Pro $99/mo); the 2-hour free-tier delay is 'the whole game' for serious reactive PR
Wire distribution: press releases pushed to newswires for indexable pickup (low authority, but persistent entity corroboration)
key_facts.note: evidence gap: exact current per-release wire pricing (PR Newswire/Business Wire) for music announcements not pulled from live pricing pages - could not verify

key_facts.claim: Pricing: music publicists charge flat fees from 'a few hundred to several thousand dollars monthly' (DJBooth); 2026 PR broadly: boutique agencies $3,000-$10,000/mo; freelancers $1,500-$3,500/mo retainer or $150-$500/hr; mid-size agencies $10,000-$25,000/mo; projects $5,000-$25,000

Unit economics: the retainer buys labor hours - at ~$333/hr billed for a senior AE, a $3,000/mo boutique retainer ~= ~9-15 hours of real work monthly (blended with junior time); tools are the smallest line item (Muck Rack $5,000+/user/yr, Qwoted Pro $149/mo); margin comes from leverage - one publicist runs multiple retainers

Retainer hour-split model (~20% strategy/angle work, 30% media-list research + pitch drafting, 30% sending + follow-ups + relationship maintenance, 20% monitoring + reporting) is a model, not a quote - firms do not publish hour splits
key_facts.note: treat as a model, not a quote

key_facts.claim: Infrastructure: the PR firm owns almost no infrastructure - it is a labor + rented-data + relationships business; journalist data lives on the vendors' servers under annual SaaS contracts (when the contract ends, the data stays with the vendor); coverage artifacts live on publishers' domains
Relationship data (who answers, what they cover, response history, warm introductions) in the firm's CRM/pitch logs is the closest thing to proprietary data in PR

Genuinely proprietary: almost nothing technical - the moats are (a) the journalist relationship graph in the publicist's head/CRM, (b) taste and news judgment, (c) reputation that gets emails opened; none of these are purchasable software

Rebuildable at zero cost - nearly the entire stack: media-list building via free sources (outlet mastheads, journalist Twitter/X bios, Substack directories, Spotify editorial team pages); pitching via any email client with a tracking spreadsheet; press-kit assembly with free design tools; monitoring via Google Alerts + free Talkwalker alerts; reactive pitching via Connectively (free tier) and Featured.com (free tier); paid databases buy speed and completeness, not capability - a determined indie team can hand-build a 100-contact genre media list in a weekend

What you cannot replicate for free: the publicist's open-rate (relationships) and the judgment of which 10 of 100 contacts matter - that is the actual product; everything else is workflow anyone can copy

Amplification: press quotes become ad creative and pitch social proof (raising Meta auction quality scores); reviews/placements drive search visibility and Wikipedia/knowledge-panel eligibility; editorial co-signs feed Spotify editorial playlist consideration indirectly (editors read press); coverage gives playlist curators and radio programmers a reason to say yes

Bid strategies: Lowest Cost, Cost Cap, Bid Cap, ROAS Target; pricing is second-price-like (VCG), so winners pay below their bid
The delivery algorithm reads ad engagement (views, clicks, comments - negative comments count as engagement) to narrow delivery; creative 'self-selects' audience as interest targeting narrows
Press/editorial coverage gives retargeting creative fresh angles and social proof, lowering CPC through higher engagement rates (which feed the auction's quality component)

attrs.description: Custom Audiences, Lookalikes, genre-level interest targeting (post-Jan-2026 consolidation), and retargeting layers with exclusions.

key_facts.claim: Custom Audiences (pixel visitors, click-throughs), Lookalikes (1% US ~= 2.3M people), interest targeting (genre-level since Jan 2026 consolidation), retargeting layers with exclusions

Practitioner workflow: prospecting ad sets (lookalike/interest) -> smart link -> retargeting ad set (visitors minus converters) with new creative -> lookalike expansion as seeds grow; retargeting converts at 2-3x cold
First-party seed data: email lists, past converter pools for lookalikes (>=1,000 click-throughs needed for a usable seed)

Rebuildable: lookalike logic approximated by manually finding similar artists' audiences (interest targeting is now genre-level anyway, which anyone can select); retargeting logic replicable via email capture on the landing page - own the list instead of renting the pool

attrs.description: The supply-side discovery surface: genre filters, follower/listener stats, approval rates, curator quotes, genre-match sliders, share-rate labels.

key_facts.claim: Genre filters, follower/listener stats, approval rates, curator quotes on what they want, genre-match sliders (SubmitHub), share-rate labels on Groover ('High' >15%, 'Very Selective' <4%)

Curator-supplied data (playlist follower counts, listener averages, genre preferences, historical approval/share rates, response times, review quality scores) is the supply-side data asset - the platform's proprietary dataset for matching and tiering
Rebuildable: Spotify playlist search + Instagram/TikTok + blog hunting builds a target list for free - this is exactly what SubmitHub's directory productizes

key_facts.claim: Artist-selected matching (SubmitHub, Groover) vs. platform-matched (Playlist Push genre-matching automation; SoundCampaign genre/budget matching)
Matching is genre-tag similarity + historical acceptance data; none publish a true ML model - it is rules + historical stats
Filter sliders and genre-match scores assist manual selection (SubmitHub)

attrs.description: The core transaction flow: upload/link track -> write pitch -> pay credits/budget -> curator inbox -> listen -> decision + feedback -> credit refund if SLA missed.

key_facts.claim: Flow: upload/link track -> write pitch -> pay credits/budget -> curator inbox -> listen -> decision + feedback -> credit refund if SLA missed

Curator workflow: listen (>=~60s required on SubmitHub premium) -> approve (add to playlist, optionally share) or decline with written reason; low-effort declines hurt curator rating and future submission flow
SubmitHub: per-curator submission -> decision + written feedback (>=10-20 words on decline) within the premium SLA window; credit refunded if SLA missed
Playlist Push: managed campaign (2-4 weeks) -> per-curator qualitative reviews; if Spotify for Artists is connected, a detailed report 30 days after the campaign ends
Dashboard: campaign status, per-curator decisions/feedback, approval rates, spend; Spotify-side verification happens in the artist's own Spotify for Artists (source-of-stream)

attrs.description: The money plumbing: SubmitHub credits (never expire), Grooviz (EUR 1 each), Playlist Push campaign budgets, SoundCampaign pay-per-completed-review; SLA clocks trigger automatic refunds.

key_facts.claim: SubmitHub credits (never expire); Grooviz (EUR 1 each); Playlist Push campaign budgets; SoundCampaign pay-per-completed-review
Artist Protection Fund (Playlist Push) / Artist Protection Program (SoundCampaign) auto-refund unfulfilled reviews to account balance
SLA automation: response clocks (48-72h SubmitHub premium; 7 days Groover; 2-4 weeks Playlist Push) trigger automatic credit refunds - the 'guarantee' is enforced by the ledger, not by humans
Free premium-credit routes on SubmitHub: Hot or Not, Verified Reviewers, referrals; free Standard credits (2 per 4 hours) for testing

attrs.description: The supply-side workbench: review queue, reputation scores, payout ledger.

key_facts.claim: Review queue, reputation scores, payout ledger (PayPal cash-out at $10 threshold on SubmitHub, per 2017 documentation)
Curator earnings: $1-$5 per review (SubmitHub, by tier/traffic) - curator payouts are the platform's COGS; the margin is in aggregation

attrs.description: AI-music detection, fake-follower monitoring, curator tiering with demotion, and application vetting - protecting the ROI loop from botted placements.

key_facts.claim: AI-music detection: SubmitHub's free AI Song Checker (labels/blocks likely-AI tracks at 85%+), Groover self-declare checkbox + curator opt-out tags

Playlist Push monitoring for fake/inactive followers and multiple accounts; curator tiering with demotion for lapsed standards (SubmitHub 2026: 4-credit top tier is earned, 30-day grace before demotion)
Vetting: curator applications reviewed for platform reach and authenticity before approval (SubmitHub)
Quality risk: low-quality/botted playlists produce streams Spotify may discount or penalize - manipulation can get music removed (Playlist Push's own warning)

attrs.description: The rented contact layer: Cision (1M+ contacts, full suite, annual contracts) or Muck Rack (profiles, pitch tracking, AI list building); the firm rents access, the vendor keeps the data.

key_facts.claim: Cision: 1M+ journalist contacts, full PR suite (database, distribution, monitoring, analytics); expensive, annual contracts, complex
Muck Rack: journalist profiles, pitch tracking, monitoring, AI list building; added press-release distribution in 2025
The firm rents access; when the contract ends, the data stays with the vendor

Rebuildable: media-list building via free sources (outlet mastheads, journalist Twitter/X bios, Substack directories, Spotify editorial team pages); a determined indie team can hand-build a 100-contact genre media list in a weekend - paid databases buy speed and completeness, not capability

attrs.description: The core labor: personalized pitches, follow-up sequences, relationship management - Muck Rack automates the plumbing, not the pitch.

key_facts.claim: Workflow: build media list (database query by beat/genre/outlet) -> draft pitch + press release -> send personalized pitches -> follow-up cadence -> log responses in pitch tracker -> monitor coverage -> compile monthly report
Core labor sold by retainers: strategy, media-list building, pitching, follow-ups, reporting
Muck Rack's pitch tracking + AI list building automate the plumbing; the pitch itself and the relationship are human
Rebuildable: pitching via any email client with a tracking spreadsheet; the paid databases buy speed and completeness, not capability

Qwoted: free 2 pitches/mo with 2-hour delay; Pro $149/mo - the 2-hour delay on free Qwoted is 'the whole game' (paid tier required for serious reactive PR)
Featured.com: free 3 submissions/mo; Pro $99/mo
Reactive workflow: scan journalist requests daily -> respond within the window
Rebuildable at zero cost: Connectively (free tier) and Featured.com (free tier)

attrs.description: Coverage tracking, share of voice, sentiment, monthly reports; AVE is legacy and rejected by measurement bodies.

key_facts.claim: Coverage tracking, share of voice, sentiment, monthly reports
Legacy metric AVE (advertising value equivalency) still auto-calculated by tools like Muck Rack but rejected by AMEC's Barcelona Principles 4.0 and banned by CIPR (2017)

Industry guidance: replace AVE with sentiment trajectory, message pull-through, share of voice, and coverage quality weighted by outlet relevance - because a big number in the wrong outlet is worthless
Rebuildable: monitoring via Google Alerts + free Talkwalker alerts; coverage reporting as a simple clippings doc with reach numbers from outlet media kits

evidence.claim: Anatomy indexed from 'Digital Anatomy of Four Music-Marketing Machines' research report (2026-10-03); per-fact evidence tiers and sources recorded in attrs.key_facts

attrs.description: Paid reach (Marquee/Showcase clicks, Discovery Mode boosts) seeds saves/follows/adds - the signals Spotify's free algorithm (Discover Weekly, Release Radar, Radio) feeds on.

key_facts.claim: Why paid reach matters: Marquee/Showcase clicks produce saves, playlist adds, follows, and catalog streams - all inputs to Spotify's organic recommendation systems (Discover Weekly, Release Radar, Radio); paid reach seeds the signals the free algorithm feeds on

Discovery Mode flywheel: boosted Radio/Autoplay exposure -> new listeners -> on-demand/catalog streams at full royalty (only DM-context streams take the 30% cut) -> stronger algorithmic profile; industry analyses estimate 100-400% stream lifts during active campaigns

The Kit's own page positions Discovery Mode as the tool for 'trending' songs; social/press signals (TikTok virality, editorial coverage) amplify by raising baseline demand that Marquee retargeting and Discovery Mode then harvest

attrs.description: Meta ad -> smart-link click -> in-Spotify actions (save/follow/playlist-add) -> Release Radar/Discover Weekly/Radio; listeners bought on Meta compound inside Spotify.

key_facts.claim: Listeners acquired via Meta who save/follow/playlist-add feed Release Radar, Discover Weekly, Radio - the same algorithmic surfaces Discovery Mode buys into; practitioners explicitly pair Meta ads with playlisting so paid listeners trigger algorithmic pickup
Social graph: shares, comments, and UGC (TikTok/Reels using the track's official audio) amplify creative beyond paid reach; retargeting pools capture the spillover
Press/editorial coverage gives retargeting creative fresh angles and social proof, lowering CPC through higher engagement rates (which feed the auction's quality component)

attrs.description: Independent playlist adds generate real streams -> saves/follows -> algorithmic systems; the entire ROI logic of pay-for-review marketplaces.

key_facts.claim: Why playlist adds matter: independent playlist placements generate real streams -> saves/follows -> feed Spotify's algorithmic systems (Release Radar, Discover Weekly, Radio); this is the entire ROI logic - paid curator access buys seeds for algorithmic compounding, same as Meta ads
Feedback as product: even declined submissions return written curator feedback - market intelligence on why a track isn't landing, which artists reuse across campaigns

key_facts.claim: Press quotes become ad creative and pitch social proof (raising Meta auction quality scores); reviews/placements drive search visibility and Wikipedia/knowledge-panel eligibility; editorial co-signs feed Spotify editorial playlist consideration indirectly (editors read press); coverage gives playlist curators and radio programmers a reason to say yes
Journalists and outlets amplify on their own socials; artist reshares multiply reach
Coverage quality is weighted by outlet relevance - a big number in the wrong outlet is worthless

attrs.description: The genuinely proprietary asset: petabyte-scale listener behavior data on Spotify's GCP tenant - who listens to what, how often, with what intensity; never leaves Spotify.

key_facts.claim: Listener behavior graph: stream counts, intentional vs. programmed streams, saves, playlist adds, skips, follows, recency/frequency/intensity per listener - this is what builds the six audience segments

All campaign, billing, targeting, and listening data lives on Spotify's infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform (2016 migration from owned data centers); the listener-affinity graph never leaves Spotify's tenant; there is no public API exposing campaign targeting or the affinity graph
Artist-visible data surfaces only through Spotify for Artists and its exports
The in-app placement and the ranking influence are the product - no third party can serve a Marquee or trigger Discovery Mode's ranking signal

The auction and its inventory; modeled attribution - a meaningful share of reported conversions are modeled, not measured, with no flag distinguishing them
Hashed identifiers (SHA-256 email/phone) are sent to Meta; Meta matches against its identity graph
No open-source stack reproduces 'find people statistically likely to click through to Spotify'

The vetted curator network itself: thousands of relationships, historical acceptance/reliability data, tiering; the SLA/refund trust infrastructure - you cannot conjure 3,000 responsive curators with track records
Artists see only their own campaign dashboards; curators see only their queues; all submission, decision, feedback, pricing-tier, and reputation data lives on each platform's own servers
